deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 85-87). In the 1983-84 notes on systems of pseudo-lines, Grothendieck studies the space X of 'relative positions' of a pseudo-line or circle D with respect to an arrangement. The positions D_t are taken up to isotopy preserving the combinatorics. Within X, the 'super-singular' positions are the most degenerate ones, where D passes through a vertex of high weight. The excluded locus is in codimension 2. X̃ denotes X with these points removed, i.e. one is not allowed to cross them.

The covering. Over X there is a principal covering with group Aut Pol(D) ≅ D_{2n}, the symmetry group of the polygon Pol(D) cut out on D, with rotation subgroup D_{2n}^+. Its fibres include the set Σ_a(D) of 'circumscribed polygons', together with two other torsors Σ_s(D) and ω(D). The question is whether the monodromy π_1(X̃, D_0) → D_{2n} is surjective, which is equivalent to the covering being connected.

Previous page.
- If crossings of super-singular positions are allowed, surjectivity holds. The 'half-turn' of D around a vertex or an edge realises the reflection in that vertex or edge.
- In X̃ alone, only the edge reflections are obtained. Together with the rotations they generate one of the three index-2 subgroups, so the image has index 1 or 2.
- A half-turn around, or a crossing of, a super-singular position acts by a rotation of amplitude n+1.

This page.
1. Whether a given loop at D_0 acts trivially on Σ_a(D_0) is unaffected by allowing crossings of super-singular positions. For n odd, the crossing-or-half-turn yields an element outside the index-2 subgroup, so π_1(X̃) → D_{2n} is surjective already.
2. For n even: let l be a loop in X crossing super-singular positions ν times, and l' the loop obtained by replacing each crossing with a half-turn around it. Then l and l' have effects on Σ_a(D_0) that are equal or opposite according to the parity of ν.
3. Hence, starting from a relative position D_0 passing through a vertex s_0 of even order, modify the half-turn loop around s_0 in this way. This gives a loop in X̃ whose action on Σ(D_0) is not the identity, and in fact lies outside the index-2 subgroup.
4. Conclusion: in all cases π_1(X̃) → D_{2n} is surjective, i.e. the principal D_{2n}-covering of X̃ is connected.

The overall method is a monodromy computation via local loops around codimension-2 degenerations, comparing 'crossing' versus 'turning around' a singular stratum. This is in the spirit of Lefschetz/Zariski–van Kampen style arguments, applied to a purely combinatorial configuration space.
errors: The n even case is only sketched. The claim that crossing and half-turn effects differ by a sign controlled by the parity of ν is asserted, not proved.
That a vertex s_0 of even order with the needed property exists is assumed, and is not checked for every arrangement.

The notation is loose: D_{2n} is used both for Aut Pol(D) and as the target group, and the 'amplitude n+1' rotation from the previous page is not justified. The logic is a working sketch rather than a complete proof.

ideas.what: Space of relative positions of a pseudo-line/circle with respect to a pseudo-line arrangement, stratified by degeneracy (generic, singular, super-singular)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial configuration space / stratified space of pseudoline extensions; related to the extension space of oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, mutations), Goodman–Pollack, Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler (oriented matroids)

ideas.what: Principal D_{2n}-covering of the position space via the polygon cut out on D, and the question of connectedness via monodromy surjectivity
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy of a covering of a combinatorial moduli space
ideas.usually_credited_to: General technique; this specific covering is not attested in the literature as far as I know

ideas.what: Comparing loops that cross a codimension-2 degenerate stratum with loops that turn around it by a half-turn; effect equal or opposite according to parity
ideas.modern_name: Local monodromy around codimension-2 strata / removing codimension-2 loci and its effect on π_1

ideas.what: Index-2 subgroups of the dihedral group: edge reflections plus even rotations, vertex reflections plus even rotations, and the rotation subgroup

missed.claim: Connectedness of a natural principal D_{2n}-covering over the space of non-super-singular relative positions of a circle or pseudo-line with respect to a pseudo-line arrangement. Equivalently, the monodromy surjects onto the full dihedral symmetry group of the cut polygon, even when crossing the most degenerate positions is forbidden.
missed.quote: Cela prouve dans tous les cas, π_1(X̃) → D_{2n} est surjectif — i.e. le revêtement principal ... de groupe D_{2n} est connexe.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's pseudo-line project is essentially unknown. A monodromy/covering viewpoint on extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids, rather than just flip-graph connectivity, is not standard in the literature. It could interest people working on extension spaces and the MacPherson / combinatorial Grassmannian circle of questions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent, nearly finished monodromy argument within an entirely unpublished Grothendieck program on pseudo-line arrangements. The topological viewpoint, coverings over combinatorial position spaces, is somewhat unusual for that combinatorics. The individual step, however, is technical and modest.
